extra.message: The `id` request parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL SELECT statement executed via sqlite3 cursor.execute(). No parameterisation or validation is applied, allowing boolean-based blind, time-based blind and UNION SQL injection (e.g. `/?id=2 UNION ALL SELECT NULL,NULL,NULL,(SELECT password FROM users)`), leaking the whole users table including passwords.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The /login handler builds its authentication query by string concatenation: `"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='" + ... + "' AND password='" + params.get("password", "") + "'"`. The password value is not sanitised at all (only username is stripped of non-word characters), so `/login?username=admin&password=' OR '1' LIKE '1` returns rows and authenticates the attacker. This is both SQL injection and a complete authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The `comment` request parameter is interpolated with `%` string formatting into an INSERT statement executed against SQLite. A single quote in the comment terminates the literal, permitting SQL injection into the write path (stacked/altered statement content, data tampering).

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The `domain` request parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to subprocess.run() with `shell=True`. Shell metacharacters are not filtered, so `/?domain=www.google.com; id` executes arbitrary OS commands as the server user (remote code execution).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message:
The `object` request parameter is passed straight to pickle.loads(). Python pickle is not a safe format: a crafted payload using the `os.system` reduce opcode (e.g. `cos
system

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: The `include` request parameter selects a file or URL whose contents are read and then passed to exec(). An attacker can point it at a remote URL (`/?include=https://pastebin.com/raw/...`) or a local file and have arbitrary Python executed in the server process, yielding remote code execution. The query string is even exposed to the injected program via the `envs` dict.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('Remote File Inclusion')

extra.message: The `path` request parameter is passed to os.abspath()/open() with no confinement to a base directory and no allowlist. `os.path.abspath` only normalises the path, it does not restrict it, so `/?path=../../../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path reads arbitrary files readable by the server user (including the application's own source, `/?path=dsvw.py`).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: If the `path` parameter contains '://' it is fetched with urllib.request.urlopen() and the response body is returned to the client. There is no scheme allowlist or destination filtering, so the server can be coerced into requesting internal/loopback services (e.g. `/?path=http://127.0.0.1:631`) or local files via `file://`, i.e. Server-Side Request Forgery.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: The `xml` request parameter is parsed with lxml using an XMLParser explicitly configured with `load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False`, and the serialised result is returned to the client. This allows XML External Entity attacks reading local files (`<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">`) and outbound network requests (SSRF via remote entities), as well as entity-expansion denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The `name` request parameter is interpolated into an XPath expression (`.//user[name/text()='%s']`) evaluated against the users XML document. A quote breaks out of the literal, allowing blind XPath injection to extract other nodes such as the admin password, e.g. `/?name=admin' and substring(password/text(),3,1)='n`.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: The `v` request parameter is substituted into the HTML footer via re.sub() and written to the response without HTML escaping (the response Content-Type is text/html). `/?v=0.4<script>alert(1)</script>` executes attacker JavaScript in the victim's browser — reflected Cross-Site Scripting. The handler additionally sends `X-XSS-Protection: 0`, disabling browser mitigation.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Comments supplied via `/?comment=<script>...` (stored at line 50) are rendered back into the comments table HTML with plain `%s` interpolation and no escaping. Every visitor of `/?comment=` executes the stored payload — stored Cross-Site Scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The inline script in HTML_PREFIX takes the `lang=` value out of `document.location.hash`, decodes it with decodeURIComponent() and injects it into the page with `document.write()`. extra.message: The `charset` request parameter is inserted directly into the Content-Type response header without stripping CR/LF. extra.message: The `size` request parameter is converted to int and used as both dimensions of a generated string (`"#" * size` repeated `size` times), so memory and CPU grow quadratically with an attacker-supplied number and there is no upper bound. `/?size=9999999` exhausts server memory — unauthenticated denial of service.

CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: The global exception handler returns `traceback.format_exc()` (or raw subprocess output) to the HTTP client. Any triggered error — e.g. `/?path=foobar` — discloses full filesystem paths, source code lines and internal state to unauthenticated users, aiding further exploitation (full path disclosure).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The comment-creation operation is a state-changing write performed on a GET request with no CSRF token, origin/referer check, or SameSite-protected session requirement. Any third-party page can force a victim's browser to post content (e.g. ``), giving Cross-Site Request Forgery.

cwe: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)

extra.message: The /login endpoint performs unlimited credential checks: there is no rate limiting, no per-account lockout, no delay, no CAPTCHA and no counter of failed attempts anywhere in the request path (the handler has no middleware — ReqHandler.do_GET is the entire pipeline). An attacker can brute-force the small plaintext password set at full request rate.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Successful and failed authentication attempts at /login produce no security audit record. The only logging is BaseHTTPRequestHandler's default access line; there is no middleware, hook or logger anywhere in the file that records auth outcomes, session issuance, or sensitive data access (/users.json, file reads). Brute-force and account-takeover activity is therefore undetectable and non-attributable.

cwe: CWE-778: Insufficient Logging

extra.message: The /users.json endpoint dumps the account directory (usernames and surnames from USERS_XML) to any unauthenticated caller. No session, token or authorization check exists on this route — nor on any of the file-read, command, deserialization or SQL routes at lines 30-61 — so all functionality is reachable without authentication.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The SESSIONID issued after successful login is generated with `random.sample(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 20)`, i.e. the non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG, and `sample` draws without replacement (further shrinking the keyspace). Session identifiers are therefore predictable from observed outputs, enabling session hijacking. A CSPRNG (secrets module) is required.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: The session cookie is set via `<meta http-equiv="Set-Cookie" content="SESSIONID=...; path=/">` with no HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite attributes. The cookie is thus readable by JavaScript (trivially stolen through the XSS sinks at lines 33, 54 and 65), transmitted over cleartext HTTP, and attached to cross-site requests.

CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Every response explicitly sends `X-XSS-Protection: 0`, deliberately turning off browser XSS auditing, and no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or X-Content-Type-Options headers are ever set.
